Tosafot on Bava Batra 141b:3:1.hebrew: נכסי להאי דמעברת - בשכיב מרע איירי, מדקאמר עלה: "ולוקמה כר' יוחנן בן ברוקה", ורבי יוחנן בן ברוקה בשכיב מרע איירי, מדקא בעי לעיל (בבא בתרא דף קלא.) עליה: "בבריא היאך?". ואע"ג דדברי שכיב מרע ככתובין וכמסורין דמו, לא מהני מידי, כיון דבבריא לא מהני אפילו ע"י קנין. ואע"ג דאמר לקמן (בבא בתרא דף קמח.): שכ"מ שאמר "הלואתו לפלוני" - הלואתו לפלוני, אע"ג דליתיה בבריא אפילו בקנין (דאי איתיה בבריא בקנין, אם כן הוי שכיב מרע ובריא שוין), מ"מ הכא ליתא בשכ"מ, כיון דליתא בבריא בקנין; דכולהו לא בחדא מחתא מחתינהו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 141b:3:1.english: "My property to this one with which you are pregnant" - It is speaking of a person who is deathly ill (shekhiv mera), since [the Gemara] says about it, "Let him establish it like Rabbi Yochanan ben Berokah," and Rabbi Yochanan ben Berokah is speaking of a deathly ill person, since [the Gemara] asks about him above (Bava Batra 131a): "[And what is the law] for a healthy person?" And even though the words of a deathly ill person are considered as if written and delivered, [his statement] is not effective at all, since for a healthy person it is not effective even by means of a kinyan (formal act of acquisition). And even though it says below (Bava Batra 148a) that if a deathly ill person said, "His loan [is given] to so-and-so," his loan is [given] to so-and-so — even though it is not [effective] for a healthy person, even with a kinyan (for if it were [effective] for a healthy person with a kinyan, then a deathly ill person and a healthy person would be equal) — nevertheless here it is not [effective] for a deathly ill person, since it is not [effective] for a healthy person with a kinyan; for [the Sages] did not set them all down with one and the same shovel (i.e., they did not treat all cases alike).

Tosafot on Bava Batra 141b:4:1.hebrew: איתיביה רב נחמן לרב הונא - ואם תאמר: אדפריך רב נחמן לרב הונא, תקשי ליה לנפשיה, דאית ליה לקמן "המזכה לעובר לא קנה"? וי"ל דהוא מוקי מתניתין לכשתלד, דסבירא ליה לקמן לכשתלד קנה. אי נמי, רב נחמן איירי בעובר שאינו בנו, ומוקי מתניתין בבנו, דדעתו של אדם קרובה אצל בנו, כר' יוחנן לקמן. וכן פסקו רבינו חננאל ורשב"ם, וה"ג דבבנו המזכה לעובר קנה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 141b:4:1.english: Rav Nachman raised an objection to Rav Huna - And if you ask: Since Rav Nachman refutes Rav Huna, he should [also] challenge himself, for he holds later [in the Gemara], "One who confers [ownership] to a fetus has not effected acquisition"? And one can answer that he [Rav Nachman] interprets the Mishnah as referring to [a gift stated as taking effect] "when she gives birth," for he holds later that [in a case of] "when she gives birth," [the fetus] does acquire. Alternatively, Rav Nachman is speaking of a fetus that is not [the giver's] son, and he interprets the Mishnah as referring to his own son, since a person's mind is close to his son, in accordance with R. Yochanan later. And so Rabbeinu Chananel and the Rashbam ruled, and so too [we conclude] that in the case of one's son, one who confers [ownership] to a fetus does effect acquisition:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 141b:7:1.hebrew: דתנן העובר פוסל ואין מאכיל - פירש רשב"ם: פוסל עבדי אביו מלאכול בתרומה, דעובר במעי אמו זר; ואינו מאכיל את אמו, דילוד מאכיל, ושאינו ילוד אינו מאכיל. ורש"י פירש ביבמות (דף סז.) בענין אחר: פוסל את אמו כהנת, אם הוא זר; ואינו מאכיל את אמו, אם הוא כהן במעי זרה, דעובר במעי זרה זר הוא. ולהאי פירוש לא מוכח הכא מידי. אבל אין לפרש כלל: פוסל עבדי אביו אם הוא זר במעי כהנת, ואינו מאכיל עבדי אביו אם הוא כהן במעי זרה, דחדא מילתא היא; דהא פשיטא דכיון דאם הוא כהן אינו מאכיל, כ"ש אם הוא ישראל, ולא הוה ליה למיתני "פוסל" אלא "אינו מאכיל":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 141b:7:1.english: "For we learned: A fetus disqualifies but does not enable [others] to eat" - Rashbam explained: It disqualifies its father's slaves from eating terumah, since a fetus in its mother's womb is [considered] a non-priest; and it does not enable its mother to eat, because a [fully] born child enables [others] to eat, but one who is not yet born does not enable [others] to eat. And Rashi explained in Yevamot (67a) in a different way: It disqualifies its mother, a priest's daughter, if it is a non-priest; and it does not enable its mother to eat, if it is a priest [conceived] in the womb of a non-priestly woman, since a fetus in the womb of a non-priestly woman is a non-priest. According to this explanation, nothing is proven here. But it cannot be explained at all [as follows]: It disqualifies its father's slaves if it is a non-priest in the womb of a priest's daughter, and it does not enable its father's slaves to eat if it is a priest in the womb of a non-priestly woman, because these are one and the same point; for it is obvious that since, if it is a priest, it does not enable [them] to eat, all the more so if it is an Israelite [it does not]. And [the Mishnah] should have taught only "does not enable to eat," not "disqualifies."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 141b:9:1.hebrew: ולימא ליה ר' יוחנן בן ברוקה היא - תימה: דאמאי נקט רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, דאפילו רבנן מודו דבלשון מתנה מועיל? ויש לומר: דכיון דראוי ליורשו, והוא לא הזכיר לשון מתנה, אם כן בירושה קאמר:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 141b:9:1.english: "And let him say to him: It is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka" - This is puzzling: Why did [the Gemara] mention Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, when even the Rabbis agree that [a transfer] by the language of a gift is effective? And one can say: Since [the unborn child] is fit to inherit from him, and he did not use the language of a gift, it follows that he is speaking of inheritance.
